Interactive Delivery Journey
The Roadmap to
National Scale

Select a phase to explore milestones in detail. Click any milestone to expand the full strategic context. The journey runs from concept design through to national and international recognition.

📅 Summer 2026 — Phase 01

Scoping & Design

The foundational phase. Partnership agreements are confirmed, academic specialists appointed, and the AI Readiness Diagnostic deployed. Curriculum framework design and regulatory engagement run in parallel with digital product prototyping.

📌
Partnership Agreement Finalised
Museum of the Future, EIG, and SIB Consulting formal agreement confirmed.
Establishes governance roles, intellectual property, brand use, financial terms, and delivery responsibilities across all three lead organisations. The foundation for all subsequent work and a prerequisite for regulatory engagement.
🎓
Academic Specialists Appointed
UAE-based pedagogical and curriculum advisors confirmed across all age phases.
Specialists provide age-phase design oversight, sustainability integration, assessment quality control, and national standard alignment. Critical for regulatory credibility with KHDA and ADEK from the outset.
🔍
AI Readiness Diagnostic Deployed
Structural assessment of infrastructure, pedagogical, and cyber-resilience gaps across initial schools.
The diagnostic surfaces school-level capability gaps before any lab rollout — enabling better-informed decisions on pacing, support needs, and Future Learning Lab placement priority.
📄
Curriculum Framework Designed
Cross-curricular AI integration model developed for K–16 aligned to national standards.
Covers all nine platform components with age-phase differentiation. Reviewed by academic specialists and aligned to KHDA, ADEK, and MoE requirements before any classroom deployment.
🏛
KHDA Regulatory Engagement Begins
Formal submission planning initiated with KHDA for the 2026–27 development cycle.
Early regulatory engagement reduces risk of implementation delays at pilot launch. KHDA pathway covers framework approval, data governance, tool vetting, and compliance reporting for Dubai schools.
📱
Digital Product Prototyping
Initial concepts for student inquiry portals, teacher dashboards, and parent apps tested.
Prototypes tested with a small group of educators and parents. Feedback informs final product specifications before pilot programme build. Includes credential engine and regulator portal designs.
🏫
Lab Environment Concept Design
Physical and digital Future Learning Lab specifications finalised for pilot schools.
Covers spatial design, approved AI toolset, hardware requirements, connectivity standards, cyber-resilience baseline, and Museum thematic alignment. Produces a replicable template for Phase Two rollout.
📅 September 2027 — Phase 02

Pilot Programme

Strategic launch across 20 targeted schools. This phase tests the diagnostic, labs, Fellow certification, and classroom AI integration in live settings. Dashboards and structured review refine the national scale model.

🏫
Strategic Launch: 20 Schools
Pilot programme activated across a targeted cohort of 20 Dubai schools.
Schools selected based on Readiness Diagnostic results, geographic spread, school type diversity — KHDA-rated, international, Arabic-medium — and leadership appetite. Diversity ensures a robust evidence base for national scale.
💻
Future Learning Labs Activated
Branded lab environments deployed and operational across all 20 pilot schools.
Each lab equips students with an approved agentic AI stack, Museum-linked challenge access, and teacher-controlled visibility tools. Physical and digital layers operate in tandem from day one.
🎓
Future Learning Fellows Certified: 2 Clusters
First cohort certified and deployed — 2 clusters × 10 schools each.
Each Fellow supports 10 schools in their cluster — providing pedagogical quality, cross-curricular AI facilitation, and frontline quality continuity. Certification pathway designed with UAE academic specialists to national standards.
🤖
Cross-Curricular AI Integration Live
Agentic AI deployed across subject areas from kindergarten to age 16.
AI moves beyond the computer lab — supporting inquiry in literature, science, history, design, and more. Human oversight and teacher controls are active at all times. Age-appropriate scaffolding reviewed and signed off.
📊
Live Dashboards & Review Processes Active
Impact dashboards live for school leaders and regulators from launch day.
Dashboards deliver real-time data on tool adoption, ethical compliance, student engagement, and Fellow performance. Review cycles at 6 and 12 weeks inform ongoing refinements before national scale.
🏅
First Micro-Credentials Issued
Museum-linked micro-credentials awarded to the first cohort of completing students.
Credentials are transportable, nationally recognised, and linked to documented learning evidence. First issuance is a significant public moment — an opportunity for Museum-led visibility and media engagement.
📈
Scale Model Refined from Evidence
Pilot learnings used to finalise national rollout architecture for Phase Three.
Covers lab design refinements, Fellow cluster sizing, tool performance data, regulatory feedback, and assessment quality findings. Output: a documented, tested model ready for Abu Dhabi, Sharjah, and national expansion.
📅 2028 Onwards — Phase 03

National Rollout

Systematic scaling across the K–16 ecosystem. The cluster model expands into Abu Dhabi, Sharjah, and the Northern Emirates under unified approvals from ADEK, SPEA, and the Ministry of Education.

🌐
Systematic K–16 Ecosystem Scaling
Cluster model replicated at national scale using the validated pilot framework.
Each new emirate cohort begins with the Readiness Diagnostic and follows the same structured pathway. Quality consistency is maintained through Fellow certification and centralised dashboard oversight.
🏛
Abu Dhabi Expansion (ADEK)
Full programme deployment across Abu Dhabi schools under ADEK approval.
ADEK pathway leverages pilot evidence and KHDA approval precedent. Regulatory submission covers framework approval, data governance, tool vetting, and reporting standards specific to Abu Dhabi's school system.
🏛
Sharjah & Northern Emirates (SPEA)
Programme extended to Sharjah and Northern Emirates under SPEA oversight.
SPEA engagement builds on Abu Dhabi evidence. Regional cultural and curriculum adaptations addressed through academic specialists with northern emirates experience. Completes the national footprint.
📘
Ministry of Education National Approval
MoE framework approval secures cross-emirate platform legitimacy and endorsement.
National approval converts the platform from a multi-emirate programme into a nationally endorsed model — strengthening international positioning, attracting research partnerships, and enabling exportable credentialing.
🔬
Research Publications Released
Peer-reviewed research from pilot and rollout phases published internationally.
Research positions the UAE as a serious contributor to the global AI-in-education knowledge base. Publication strategy targets high-impact journals and international education conferences.
🏆
International Recognition Secured
Platform recognised as the world-first benchmark for AI-integrated future education.
International recognition strategy includes OECD engagement, UNESCO dialogues, bilateral education partnerships, and participation in global futures-of-education forums. The Museum of the Future is the natural host for a flagship international event.
🌟
Global Benchmark Established
The UAE Future Learning Platform becomes the international reference model.
Other nations look to the UAE's model as the template for combining national AI policy, cultural institutions, school infrastructure, and measurable outcomes in one coherent framework. Better intelligence. Better decisions. Better outcomes.

National Context
Why Now Matters
More Than Ever

The UAE Cabinet's decision to embed artificial intelligence across all school years signals more than curriculum reform. It signals a wider shift in how the nation understands human capability, future readiness, and the role of public institutions in preparing young people for a rapidly changing world.

Policy intent alone does not produce educational transformation. Schools are under pressure to select tools, educators are being asked to absorb unfamiliar models of teaching and assessment, and regulators need clearer visibility into what meaningful implementation looks like in practice. Institutions that help shape the operating framework at this stage are likely to influence the national model materially.

System Challenges & Platform Responses
Turning Critical Pain Points
Into Solved Problems

The UAE's educational landscape is characterised by deep institutional silos. Translating a visionary national AI mandate into daily classroom reality exposes critical vulnerabilities. Left unaddressed, these system failures degrade a historic mandate into superficial compliance.

Challenge Why It Matters Consequence If Unaddressed Platform Response
Structural
Fragmented Implementation		 Schools operate in isolated silos, adopting disparate pedagogical models without a central, quality-assured framework. Severe inequality in future literacy outcomes across different emirates, school categories, and demographics. Response
Agentic AI Architecture & Integration — a coherent school-wide AI toolset and visibility layer subject to governance and implementation controls.
Capacity
Uneven Teacher Readiness		 AI is dismissed as a peripheral "tech add-on" rather than a cognitive tool, generating staff anxiety and resistance. Critically low adoption rates and isolation of AI concepts from core academic learning across the system. Response
Future Learning Fellows Pathway — certified capacity nodes supporting consistent quality across 10-school clusters.
Infrastructure
Disconnected Tools & Workflows		 Schools procure expensive, disconnected software subscriptions that fail to integrate with core K–12 curricula. Higher institutional cost with limited educational return. Tools lacking strategic architecture deliver inconsistent value. Response
Future Learning Digital Product Layer — purpose-built tools, apps, portals, and platforms as part of the concept architecture itself.
Governance
Lack of QA & Standards		 Absence of unified standards for how AI tools are vetted for ethical design, safety, and educational suitability. Elevated exposure to data privacy risks, algorithmic bias, and poorly evaluated classroom applications at scale. Response
Governance by Design — ethics-first tool approval, data sovereignty protocols, and regulator-ready reporting built from the outset.
Security
Cyber Attack & Digital Risk		 As schools expand their digital footprint, they increase exposure to phishing, ransomware, credential compromise, and wider cyber weaknesses. Service disruption, data loss, safeguarding concerns, reputational damage, and reduced confidence in school-based AI adoption. Response
Cyber-Resilience by Design — security review, access discipline, digital hygiene, and resilience planning baked into every implementation stage.
Measurement
Difficulty Measuring Impact		 Regulators lack live diagnostic visibility and systemic dashboards tracking capability adoption at scale. Blind spots at the national level. Inability to prove educational alignment with the AED 335 billion AI economic strategy. Response
Diagnostic & Impact Dashboards — a clearer evidence base for implementation progress, capability growth, and regulator-facing reporting.

AI Economy & Entrepreneurship
Preparing Students for
Economies That Don't Yet Exist

The platform does not just teach students about AI — it teaches them to think, create, and build with it. From kindergarten through to age 16, every age phase is designed to develop future economic actors: curious, resilient, entrepreneurially literate, and capable of generating real-world value.

🌱
Foundation · KG–Age 6

Value & Exchange

Children explore simple ideas of making, sharing, and the value of things through tactile, story-led experiences. The earliest building blocks of economic literacy and collaborative thinking.

💡
Discovery · Ages 7–11

Design for Community

Students design healthier food, energy, and mobility solutions for their community using structured AI prompts. First introduction to problem-framing, iteration, and real-world impact thinking.

📊
Application · Ages 12–14

Future Business Models

Students use supervised AI modelling to explore how ideas create public and economic value. Climate resilience, circular design, and entrepreneurship combine in structured project briefs.

🚀
Creation · Ages 15–16

Economic Readiness

Students develop and test real future-economy proposals — combining AI analysis, sustainability thinking, and entrepreneurial logic into outputs that demonstrate world-readiness at age 16.

Frequently Asked Questions
Addressing the Hard Questions
Head On

Every serious stakeholder will ask difficult questions. These are the questions we expect — and the answers that demonstrate why this platform is designed to withstand institutional scrutiny.

Is this just another AI pilot that won't scale?
No. The platform is architectured specifically to avoid the pilot trap. Phase One is scoping and design — not a premature launch. Phase Two deploys 20 schools with a deliberately documented evidence base. Phase Three uses that evidence to scale systematically. At every stage, the Readiness Diagnostic, Fellow certification model, and impact dashboards create the conditions for repeatable, quality-controlled expansion — not a one-off experiment.
How does this align with UAE curriculum standards?
Curriculum alignment is built into the concept from the outset — not retrofitted. UAE-based academic specialists are appointed in Phase One specifically to ensure the framework meets the requirements of KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, and the Ministry of Education. AI is integrated across existing subjects, not added as a competing curriculum element. Every component is reviewed for national standard compliance before any classroom deployment.
What safeguards exist for student data and privacy?
Data sovereignty, privacy, and cyber resilience are treated as non-negotiable design conditions — not afterthoughts. The platform includes verifiable protocols for data sovereignty, privacy protection, tool approval vetting, and human oversight. The Cyber Guard tool provides school-level monitoring, and the Cyber-Resilience by Design layer of the technology stack covers phishing awareness, incident response, and algorithmic bias auditing from day one of implementation.
What makes this different from existing edtech products?
Existing edtech products are tools. This is a platform — the difference is structural. Every digital product is purpose-built as part of the concept architecture, not procured independently. The platform combines physical lab environments, certified educators, museum-linked credentialing, regulator dashboards, and cross-curricular AI integration within one governed framework. No existing edtech product offers anything close to this combination at national scale.
How does the Museum benefit without doing the operational heavy lifting?
The Museum provides the strategic anchor, brand authority, thematic framework, and credentialing architecture — Ecosystem Intelligence Group leads the implementation architecture and SIB Consulting manages operational coordination. The Museum's role is designed to be high-leverage and low-operational-burden: the brand, the vision, and the credentialing power — without day-to-day programme management.
What happens if the pilot evidence is mixed?
The platform is explicitly designed to learn from the pilot, not to assume it will be perfect. Review cycles at 6 and 12 weeks during Phase Two feed directly into refinements before national scale. The diagnostic framework identifies problems early. The Fellow cluster model localises quality challenges so they don't cascade across the whole system. Mixed evidence is information — and the platform's governance architecture is built to act on it.
Why Ecosystem Intelligence Group as lead partner?
EIG brings an integrated methodology across six disciplines and a structured four-stage process designed to move multi-stakeholder complexity toward measurable outcomes. Its role is to hold together the research logic, governance architecture, design discipline, implementation framework, and scale pathway that a concept of this nature requires. EIG's approach — turning complexity into clarity — is exactly what a platform spanning regulators, schools, educators, parents, and a national cultural institution demands.
How long until we see measurable impact?
From Phase Two launch in September 2027: school adoption metrics are live from day one. First micro-credentials are issued within the first academic term. Regulator dashboard reporting is active from pilot launch. Longitudinal capability tracking begins immediately and compounds across years. The platform is designed to show evidence quickly, improve continuously, and demonstrate national impact clearly — because that visibility is itself part of the value proposition to every stakeholder.
